title: Seedless (1.51)
hook: the first chapter of the Yoga Sutras ends by letting go of the very last thing the mind holds

segments.voice: Yesterday: ritambhara, truth-bearing wisdom, the knowing that carries the truth and leaves a groove that blocks all the others. Today, the last sutra of chapter one.

A gardener clears a field. First the big weeds. Then the small ones. Then the seeds still lying in the soil, waiting to sprout. At last one seed is left: the special one she planted on purpose, the one that crowded out the weeds. The field is quiet and clean. And now, strangely, she lets that one go too. Not because it was bad. Because the field was the point all along. That's sutra 1.51, the last line of the first chapter.
screen: `THE BIG WEEDS, THE SMALL ONES.` → `ONE GOOD SEED LEFT.` → `SHE LETS THAT ONE GO TOO.`

segments.voice: Sutra 1.51: tasyapi nirodhe sarva nirodhan nirbijah samadhih. When even that is stilled, everything being stilled, there is seedless absorption. Even that: the impression left by yesterday's truth-bearing wisdom, the last good groove in the mind. When it too goes quiet, nothing is left that could sprout again. Nirbija: without seed. Vyasa explains that the mind then dissolves back into its source, and the seer, purusha, rests alone, pure and free. That loops back to the third sutra, fifteen days ago: then the seer rests in its own form. The first chapter is a circle. It began with the definition of yoga, and it ends with yoga complete. Look at the path it walked. Atha, now. The seer. The five turnings. Practice and non-attachment. Samadhi with seed, and without. The born-free and the rest of us. Or, devotion to Ishvara. Om, repeated with its meaning. The nine obstacles. One thing. The four keys. Or the breath. Many doors. Mastery, small to large. The crystal taking the color. Truth-bearing wisdom. And seedless. Seventeen sessions, from now to nothing held. This chapter is the Samadhi Pada, the part on absorption. Tomorrow begins the Sadhana Pada, the part on practice, and it starts with three simple things.
screen: `EVEN THAT IS STILLED.` · `NIRBIJA: NOTHING LEFT TO SPROUT.` · `BACK TO 1.3: THE SEER RESTS.` · `SEVENTEEN SESSIONS, FROM THE TOP.` · then, large: `SEEDLESS.`

segments.voice: Rest on the breath for a while, then, without forcing anything, loosen your grip on it too, and let it breathe itself. Sit holding nothing in particular, just aware; if a thought comes, let it go without picking up a new support. This isn't about reaching anything, only a taste of letting go of even the good seed.
Seedless. Nirbija samadhi, sutra 1.51: when even the last good impression is stilled, nothing remains that could sprout, and the seer rests in itself.
Your line: nirbija. Even the good seed, let go, and the seer rests. Chapter one, done.

screen: `DAY 446 COUNTS.` → `SAMADHI PADA, DONE.` → `TOMORROW: KRIYA YOGA — DISCIPLINE, STUDY, SURRENDER.`

howItsDone: In classical yoga, seedless samadhi is described as the culmination of practice, and students study the whole first chapter as a map from the definition of yoga in 1.2 to its completion in 1.51.

fork.setup: truth-bearing wisdom has cleared away every other impression. only its own remains. what does sutra 1.51 do with it?
options: keep it forever as the highest state.
replace it with a new seed.
fork.reveal: when even that is stilled, everything stilled, there is seedless samadhi. the last good seed goes too.

original.note: Sanskrit nirbīja: seedless. the samadhi with nothing left that could sprout again.

trapdoor: what you thought: seedless means empty, a blank.
what it means: the mind holds nothing, not even its best insight, and the seer rests in its own form.
what a scholar hears: 1.51 completes nirodha (1.2) and returns to 1.3; Vyasa says the mind dissolves into prakriti with its samskaras, and purusha abides alone, the kaivalya of the fourth chapter.
recall: one-pointed: a mind on a single object

chat.says: If truth-bearing wisdom is so good, why let it go too?
options: It's the last seed. Once even it is stilled, the seer rests in its own form.
Because it was false all along, a mistake that needs to be thrown away.
Because wisdom fades with age, so you have to start again from the top.
chat.meaning: Sutra 1.51: when even the impression of truth-bearing wisdom is stilled, absorption is seedless, and the seer rests in its own form.
